title: Helm chart: support Runtime LTS channel selection + release note URL annotations
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
## Context
Dedicated/Private customers adopting the Runtime LTS line need a stable, pin-able runtime image tag and a clear way to discover the matching release notes from the deployed manifest.

We already have the LTS branch/tagging direction (runtime-1.18-lts + patch tags like 1.18.1-lts). This ticket adds Helm chart support so Private deployments can:
1) select the LTS channel (image tags) without bespoke chart forks
2) surface release notes URLs in rendered resources via annotations (for ops audit/change control)

## Goals
- Add Helm values to select Runtime LTS images/tags.
- Support explicit pinning to an LTS patch tag (e.g., 1.18.1-lts) and prevent accidental drift.
- Add an annotation with the release notes URL on the runtime Deployment/StatefulSet (and any relevant workload resource used by the chart).
- Keep existing default behavior unchanged for non-LTS users.

## Non-goals
- Building an LTS channel controller inside the chart.
- Auto-upgrading within the LTS line.
- Hosting release notes; we only point to the canonical URL.

## Proposed Helm interface (values)
### New values
- `runtime.channel`: `stable` | `lts`
  - Default: `stable`
- `runtime.image.tag`: existing behavior (string)
  - For `runtime.channel=lts`, default should resolve to the current recommended LTS patch tag maintained by Release Eng (documented in chart values + release notes).
- `runtime.lts.patchTag`: optional explicit pin (string)
  - Example: `1.18.1-lts`
  - Precedence: if set, overrides `runtime.image.tag`.
- `runtime.releaseNotes.url`: optional override (string)
  - If unset, chart will generate a URL based on tag (when possible) OR leave empty.

### Annotation behavior
Add the following annotation(s) to the runtime workload resource (and template metadata so it is visible via `kubectl describe`):
- `redwood.ai/runtime-release-notes-url: <url>`
- `redwood.ai/runtime-channel: lts|stable`
- `redwood.ai/runtime-image-tag: <resolved-tag>`

If the URL is empty/unset, still set channel + tag annotations.

## Backwards compatibility
- Default remains `runtime.channel=stable` and does not change existing tag resolution.
- Existing `runtime.image.tag` continues to work.
- If `runtime.lts.patchTag` is set, chart should render a NOTE/WARN in `NOTES.txt` clarifying that the runtime is pinned and must be updated manually.

## Validation / test plan
- `helm template` snapshots for:
  - stable channel, explicit tag
  - lts channel, default tag
  - lts channel, pinned patchTag
  - lts channel, pinned patchTag + explicit releaseNotes.url
- Chart lint passes.
- Minimal on-cluster smoke: install/upgrade path in a dev cluster, verify:
  - annotations show on the workload
  - upgrading chart without changing pin does not change runtime image

## Release / rollout
- Ship as a minor chart version bump (new values, no breaking change).
- Update chart README/examples for Private LTS adoption.
- Coordinate with ENG-4827 (Private installer) so installer can write values for pinning + checksums verification at the installer layer.

## Links
- Helm PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr-388-add-values-for-runtime-lts-channel.json
- LTS initiative epic: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-runtime-lts-initiative-epic.json

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Helm values allow selecting LTS channel and pinning LTS patch tag
- [x] Rendered workload contains channel + tag annotations
- [x] Rendered workload contains release notes URL annotation (when provided)
- [x] Docs/examples updated
- [x] No behavior change for existing installs unless values are set
comments: 2025-01-23 (Connor O'Brien): Creating this as part of the LTS packaging surface. Dedicated is mostly handled by internal deploy tooling, but Private/Helm customers need a first-class path to select/pin LTS tags and see the matching release notes in-cluster for audit/change control.

2025-01-27 (Marissa Cole): +1 on release notes discoverability. Please ensure the annotation is on the workload template metadata (not just the top-level chart), so it survives rollout and is visible per revision.

2025-01-29 (Vivek Kulkarni): From Private perspective, we need an explicit pin field (patch tag) so the installer can write it. Avoid "latest-lts" style moving tags unless there’s a very loud warning; procurement teams will treat that as an uncontrolled change.

2025-02-03 (Bruno Silva): Drafted values schema:
- runtime.channel
- runtime.lts.patchTag
- runtime.releaseNotes.url
Implementation plan: resolve tag in `_helpers.tpl`, then apply annotations in deployment template. Will keep runtime.image.tag working as-is for stable channel.
Open question: do we want to auto-generate release notes URL from tag? I’m leaning to allowing override only (safest) and documenting the canonical pattern later once docs URL is stable.

2025-02-07 (Elliot Price): Prefer explicit URL override for now. We’ve had docs URL patterns change between doc site reorganizations; having installer/ops set it avoids stale/broken links. We can add generation later once the pattern is guaranteed.

2025-02-12 (Bruno Silva): PR up in redwood-helm-charts. Added annotations:
- redwood.ai/runtime-release-notes-url
- redwood.ai/runtime-channel
- redwood.ai/runtime-image-tag
Also added NOTES.txt message when `runtime.lts.patchTag` is set. Added helm unit-style render tests via snapshot comparisons in CI.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Request: include channel+tag annotations even when URL is missing; helps SREs confirm what’s deployed during incident triage. Also confirm annotations exist on pod template metadata so they show up per replicaset rollout.

2025-02-18 (Bruno Silva): Addressed review feedback: moved annotations to both workload metadata + pod template metadata. Leaving URL optional. Updated README with examples for `runtime.channel=lts` + pinned `runtime.lts.patchTag=1.18.1-lts` and how to set releaseNotes.url from the LTS release notes page.

2025-02-20 (Connor O'Brien): Merged. Next step is to coordinate with ENG-4827 so installer writes these values automatically for LTS installs and points releaseNotes.url to the artifact/release notes location used by Release Eng.
